claim: SYCP3 is a component of the synaptonemal complex lateral element.
source: As a component of the SC lateral element, SYCP3 has a critical role in defining the specific chromosome architecture required for correct meiotic progression.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by the broader context of the manuscript.

claim: SYCP3 has a critical role in defining the specific chromosome architecture required for correct meiotic progression.
source: As a component of the SC lateral element, SYCP3 has a critical role in defining the specific chromosome architecture required for correct meiotic progression.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract supported by the experimental work described.

claim: SYCP3 causes compaction of chromosomal DNA.
source: In the model, the reported compaction of chromosomal DNA caused by SYCP3 would result from its ability to bridge distant sites on a DNA molecule with the DNA-binding domains located at each end of its strut-like structure.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript and references to previous work.

claim: SYCP3 bridges distant sites on a DNA molecule with DNA-binding domains located at each end of its strut-like structure.
source: In the model, the reported compaction of chromosomal DNA caused by SYCP3 would result from its ability to bridge distant sites on a DNA molecule with the DNA-binding domains located at each end of its strut-like structure.
evidence: This is supported by structural data and the single-molecule experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: The synaptonemal complex mediates the synapsis of homologous chromosomes pairs during meiotic prophase I.
source: The synaptonemal complex (SC) is a dynamic proteinaceous ultra-structure that mediates the synapsis of homologous chromosomes pairs during meiotic prophase I (Cahoon and Hawley, 2016; Fraune et al., 2016; Yang and Wang, 2009; Zickler and Kleckner, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to established literature.

claim: The SC is composed of three parts: lateral elements, transverse filaments and a central element.
source: Morphologically, the SC is composed of three parts: lateral elements, transverse filaments and a central element.
evidence: This is a well-established structural description of the SC.

claim: Lateral elements are protein scaffolds that extend along the entire length of each chromosome axis.
source: Lateral elements are protein scaffolds that extend along the entire length of each chromosome axis.
evidence: This is a structural description supported by established knowledge.

claim: Transverse filaments connect the chromosomes in a homologous pair to the midline central element.
source: They become linked together by transverse filaments, which connect the chromosomes in a homologous pair to the midline central element, to induce chromosome synapsis (Schücker et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The tripartite SC ultra-structure provides an essential three-dimensional scaffold for meiotic progression.
source: The tripartite SC ultra-structure provides an essential three-dimensional scaffold for meiotic progression and its absence or defective formation can lead to failure of meiotic progression and infertility (Bolcun-Filas et al., 2007, 2009; de Vries et al., 2005; Hamer et al., 2008; Schramm et al., 2011; Yang et al., 2006; Yuan et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to studies showing the consequences of SC defects.

claim: Absence or defective formation of the SC can lead to failure of meiotic progression and infertility.
source: The tripartite SC ultra-structure provides an essential three-dimensional scaffold for meiotic progression and its absence or defective formation can lead to failure of meiotic progression and infertility (Bolcun-Filas et al., 2007, 2009; de Vries et al., 2005; Hamer et al., 2008; Schramm et al., 2011; Yang et al., 2006; Yuan et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to experimental studies.

claim: The lateral element is the first part of the synaptonemal complex to assemble.
source: The lateral element is the first part of the synaptonemal complex to assemble.
evidence: This is a statement about the temporal order of SC assembly.

claim: Lateral element formation coincides with the controlled induction of double-strand DNA breaks and subsequent homology searches.
source: In most organisms, its formation coincides with the controlled induction of double-strand DNA breaks and subsequent homology searches that bring homologous chromosomes into alignment (Baudat et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: SYCP2 and SYCP3 are the major protein components of the lateral element.
source: It is at this step that SYCP2 and SYCP3, the major protein components of the lateral element (Lammers et al., 1994; Offenberg et al., 1998; Schalk et al., 1998), assemble on the chromosome axis, in a manner dependent on each other and on the presence of meiosis-specific cohesin (Fukuda et al., 2014; Llano et al., 2012; Pelttari et al., 2001; Winters et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: SYCP2 and SYCP3 assemble on the chromosome axis in a manner dependent on each other and on the presence of meiosis-specific cohesin.
source: It is at this step that SYCP2 and SYCP3, the major protein components of the lateral element (Lammers et al., 1994; Offenberg et al., 1998; Schalk et al., 1998), assemble on the chromosome axis, in a manner dependent on each other and on the presence of meiosis-specific cohesin (Fukuda et al., 2014; Llano et al., 2012; Pelttari et al., 2001; Winters et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Male mice lacking SYCP3 are infertile as their germ cells undergo apoptosis due to failure in meiotic progression.
source: Male mice lacking SYCP3 are infertile as their germ cells undergo apoptosis due to failure in meiotic progression (Yuan et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Female mice lacking SYCP3 are sub-fertile, with increased aneuploidy leading to fetal deaths during gestation.
source: In contrast, females are sub-fertile, with increased aneuploidy leading to fetal deaths during gestation.
evidence: This is stated in the context of SYCP3 knockout mice.

claim: In SYCP3-deficient mice, the chromosome axis is twice the length of that in wild-type mice.
source: in SYCP3-deficient mice, the chromosome axis is twice the length of that in wild-type mice and cohesin disassembles prematurely (Kouznetsova et al., 2005; Yuan et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In SYCP3-deficient mice, cohesin disassembles prematurely.
source: in SYCP3-deficient mice, the chromosome axis is twice the length of that in wild-type mice and cohesin disassembles prematurely (Kouznetsova et al., 2005; Yuan et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The large-scale architecture of the meiotic chromosome consists of a regular array of DNA loops that emanate from a chromosome axis consisting of conjoined sister chromatids.
source: The large-scale architecture of the meiotic chromosome consists of a regular array of DNA loops that emanate from a chromosome axis consisting of conjoined sister chromatids (Zickler and Kleckner, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Sister chromatid cohesion is enforced at the loop base by meiotic ring-like cohesin complexes.
source: Sister chromatid cohesion is enforced at the loop base by meiotic ring-like cohesin complexes (Rankin, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: SYCP3's role is to provide local DNA compaction to modulate the existing axis-loop structure of the meiotic chromosome.
source: Thus, it is likely that SYCP3's role is to provide local DNA compaction to modulate the existing axis-loop structure of the meiotic chromosome, in the specific manner required for efficient recombination between homologues.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural and functional data presented.

claim: SYCP3 adopts a highly elongated tetrameric assembly of antiparallel α-helices.
source: Crystallographic analysis shows that SYCP3 adopts a highly elongated tetrameric assembly of antiparallel α-helices, with flexible termini protruding from the helical core.
evidence: This is based on crystallographic data from previous work.

claim: SYCP3 has flexible termini protruding from the helical core.
source: Crystallographic analysis shows that SYCP3 adopts a highly elongated tetrameric assembly of antiparallel α-helices, with flexible termini protruding from the helical core.
evidence: This is based on crystallographic data from previous work.

claim: The N-terminal sequences located at each end of the SYCP3 structure bind double-stranded DNA.
source: The N-terminal sequences located at each end of the SYCP3 structure bind double-stranded (ds) DNA, suggesting that SYCP3 can act as a 20 nm-long physical strut to hold distinct regions of DNA together.
evidence: This is based on structural and biochemical data.

claim: SYCP3 can act as a 20 nm-long physical strut to hold distinct regions of DNA together.
source: The N-terminal sequences located at each end of the SYCP3 structure bind double-stranded (ds) DNA, suggesting that SYCP3 can act as a 20 nm-long physical strut to hold distinct regions of DNA together.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural data showing DNA-binding domains at both ends.

claim: SYCP3 can polymerise into regular supra-structures resembling the SC lateral element.
source: In addition, SYCP3 can polymerise into regular supra-structures resembling the SC lateral element (Baier et al., 2007; Syrjänen et al., 2014), in a self-assembly reaction that requires both N- and C-terminal motifs.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: SYCP3 self-assembly requires both N- and C-terminal motifs.
source: In addition, SYCP3 can polymerise into regular supra-structures resembling the SC lateral element (Baier et al., 2007; Syrjänen et al., 2014), in a self-assembly reaction that requires both N- and C-terminal motifs.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The crystal structure of SYCP3 shows a tetrameric assembly with N-terminal DNA-binding domains located at both ends of the central helical core.
source: The crystal structure of SYCP3 showed a tetrameric assembly with N-terminal DNA-binding domains located at both ends of the central helical core (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is based on crystallographic data and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: SYCP31-230 is a version of SYCP3 missing the last six amino acids.
source: To study the mechanism of DNA binding separately from higher-order assembly and alleviate the limited solubility of the full-length protein, we used a version of SYCP3 missing the last six amino acids, SYCP31-230(Baier et al., 2007; Syrjänen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a description of the construct used in the experiments.

claim: SYCP31-230 was used to study the mechanism of DNA binding separately from higher-order assembly.
source: To study the mechanism of DNA binding separately from higher-order assembly and alleviate the limited solubility of the full-length protein, we used a version of SYCP3 missing the last six amino acids, SYCP31-230(Baier et al., 2007; Syrjänen et al., 2014).
evidence: This explains the rationale for using the truncated construct.

claim: Reconstitution of an SYCP3 complex with a DNA sample containing equal nucleotide concentrations of dsDNA 32- and 60mer yielded a species of intermediate mobility.
source: Reconstitution of an SYCP3 complex with a DNA sample containing equal nucleotide concentrations of dsDNA 32- and 60mer yielded a species of intermediate mobility relative to the slower SYCP3-DNA 32mer and faster SYCP3-DNA 60mer complexes, consistent with the formation of an SYCP3-DNA complex containing both lengths of dsDNA (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is based on the electrophoretic mobility shift assay shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The intermediate mobility species is consistent with the formation of an SYCP3-DNA complex containing both lengths of dsDNA.
source: Reconstitution of an SYCP3 complex with a DNA sample containing equal nucleotide concentrations of dsDNA 32- and 60mer yielded a species of intermediate mobility relative to the slower SYCP3-DNA 32mer and faster SYCP3-DNA 60mer complexes, consistent with the formation of an SYCP3-DNA complex containing both lengths of dsDNA (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the EMSA data.

claim: SYCP3 can bridge between a fluorescently-labelled dsDNA and a distinct biotin-labelled dsDNA immobilised on streptavidin-coated beads.
source: To provide further evidence of multivalent DNA binding, we showed that SYCP3 can bridge between a fluorescently-labelled dsDNA and a distinct biotin-labelled dsDNA immobilised on streptavidin-coated beads (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is based on the pull-down assay shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Binding of fluorescently-labelled SYCP3 to λ DNA in the single-molecule setup was readily observed by confocal fluorescence microscopy.
source: Binding of fluorescently-labelled SYCP3 to λ DNA in the single-molecule setup was readily observed by confocal fluorescence microscopy.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experiments.

claim: Kymographs revealed binding and one-dimensional diffusive behaviour of SYCP3 on dsDNA.
source: Kymographs, acquired from repeated confocal line-scans along the DNA, revealed binding and one-dimensional diffusive behaviour of SYCP3 on dsDNA (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on the kymograph data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: A construct lacking the N-terminal DNA-binding domain, SYCP391-230, did not interact with λ DNA.
source: As a control, a construct lacking the N-terminal DNA-binding domain, SYCP391-230, did not interact with λ DNA.
evidence: This is a control experiment demonstrating the importance of the N-terminal domain for DNA binding.

claim: When λ DNA is in an extended conformation, the majority of SYCP3 molecules interacted with DNA in a diffusive manner.
source: In the initial phase of the compaction experiment, when λ DNA is in an extended conformation, the majority of SYCP3 molecules interacted with DNA in a diffusive manner, displaying a one-dimensional sliding motion along the DNA molecule.
evidence: This is based on the single-molecule observations.

claim: SYCP3 displays a one-dimensional sliding motion along the DNA molecule when DNA is extended.
source: In the initial phase of the compaction experiment, when λ DNA is in an extended conformation, the majority of SYCP3 molecules interacted with DNA in a diffusive manner, displaying a one-dimensional sliding motion along the DNA molecule.
evidence: This is based on the single-molecule observations.

claim: The 1D-diffusion constant of SYCP3 is 0.16 ± 0.05 µm2/s.
source: Mean-squared displacement analysis of diffusive trajectories revealed a 1D-diffusion constant of 0.16 ± 0.05 µm2/s (N = 8, see Materials and methods section '1D-Diffusion coefficient analysis').
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of the diffusive trajectories.

claim: When the DNA was temporarily relaxed and then pulled taut again, the majority of diffusing SYCP3 molecules co-localised in clusters that remained static and stable over time.
source: Intriguingly, when the DNA was temporarily relaxed and then pulled taut again, a drastic alteration in SYCP3's binding behaviour was observed: the majority of diffusing SYCP3 molecules co-localised in clusters that remained static and stable over time.
evidence: This is a key observation from the single-molecule experiments.

claim: SYCP3 has two different modes of binding to DNA.
source: These findings indicate that SYCP3 has two different modes of binding to DNA.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental observations.

claim: The diffusive binding mode reflects the interaction with the extended λ DNA of a single DNA-binding domain at one end of the rigid SYCP3 strut.
source: We hypothesise that the diffusive binding mode reflects the interaction with the extended λ DNA of a single DNA-binding domain at one end of the rigid SYCP3 strut, allowing SYCP3 to slide along the DNA molecule (first-binding mode).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the structural and functional data.

claim: Upon relaxation of the DNA substrate, DNA-bound SYCP3 would engage concurrently a distinct DNA site with its other DNA-binding domain, in a bridging interaction leading to formation of a DNA loop.
source: Upon relaxation of the DNA substrate, DNA-bound SYCP3 would engage concurrently a distinct DNA site with its other DNA-binding domain, in a bridging interaction leading to formation of a DNA loop (second binding-mode).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental observations.

claim: Higher forces were required to extend λ DNA after the compaction step relative to naked DNA.
source: Consistent with the presence of SYCP3-dependent loops in the DNA that might resist extension, higher forces were required to extend λ DNA after the compaction step relative to naked DNA (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is based on force-distance measurements shown in Figure 4A.

claim: SYCP3-dependent DNA bridges did not exhibit extensive and distinct bond-rupture events.
source: In our experiments, SYCP3-dependent DNA bridges did not exhibit extensive and distinct bond-rupture events (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), as previously observed for DNA-bridging proteins H-NS and Alba1 (Dame et al., 2006; Laurens et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on the force-distance data and comparison to other DNA-bridging proteins.

claim: The lack of pronounced rupture events suggests a comparatively high stability of SYCP3-compacted DNA.
source: The lack of pronounced rupture events suggests a comparatively high stability of SYCP3-compacted DNA, although further quantitative analysis would require quadruple optical trapping experiments (Heller et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The SYCP3 cluster size was distributed around a mean value of 67 tetramers per cluster.
source: After correction for bleaching (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), we determined that the SYCP3 cluster size was distributed around a mean value of 67 tetramers per cluster, with individual clusters showing a range of 20 to 160 tetramers (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of the fluorescence data.

claim: Individual SYCP3 clusters show a range of 20 to 160 tetramers.
source: After correction for bleaching (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), we determined that the SYCP3 cluster size was distributed around a mean value of 67 tetramers per cluster, with individual clusters showing a range of 20 to 160 tetramers (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of the fluorescence data.

claim: The DNA-binding footprint of SYCP3 is 2.7 nm ± 1.7 nm.
source: Combining the quantification of the number of SYCP3 tetramers in a cluster with a measure of the reduction in DNA length caused by SYCP3-dependent compaction yielded an estimate of 2.7 nm ± 1.7 nm (N = 3) for the DNA-binding footprint of SYCP3 (see Materials and methods, section 'SYCP3 footprint calculation') (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis combining cluster size and DNA compaction measurements.

claim: In experiments where flow drag was used to establish micrometer-long sections of DNA molecules bridged by SYCP3, an apparent footprint value of 3.6 ± 0.3 nm was obtained.
source: In a different set of experiments, where flow drag was used to establish micrometer-long sections of DNA molecules bridged by SYCP3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 4), we obtained an apparent footprint value of 3.6 ± 0.3 nm (N = 13).
evidence: This is based on a different experimental approach shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: The footprint value of SYCP3 is close to the size of one helical turn of DNA.
source: This footprint value, close to the size of one helical turn of DNA, is in broad agreement with the expected size of the SYCP3-binding site.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the footprint measurements.

claim: Transient bridging events might form the basis of SYCP3's ability to compact chromosomal DNA in meiosis.
source: The observed tendency of SYCP3 to accumulate in discrete clusters on dsDNA might form the basis of its ability to compact chromosomal DNA in meiosis.
evidence: This is an interpretation connecting the in vitro observations to the in vivo function.

claim: Formation of a transient DNA loop by a single bridging event would facilitate further bridging interactions of neighbouring SYCP3 tetramers.
source: Of note, formation of a transient DNA loop by a single bridging event would by itself facilitate further bridging interactions of neighbouring SYCP3 tetramers, even in the absence of cooperative protein-protein interactions (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a mechanistic hypothesis supported by theoretical considerations.

claim: A mechanism of DNA compaction driven by the reduced entropic penalty of successive DNA-bridging events has been predicted by molecular dynamics studies.
source: Such a mechanism of DNA compaction, driven by the reduced entropic penalty of successive DNA-bridging events, has been predicted by molecular dynamics studies (Brackley et al., 2013; Cheng et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to theoretical studies.

claim: Apparently cooperative DNA-binding behavior of DNA-bridging proteins has been attributed to the induced proximity of distinct protein-bound DNA sites in previous studies.
source: Apparently cooperative DNA-binding behavior of DNA-bridging proteins has been attributed to the induced proximity of distinct protein-bound DNA sites in previous studies (Dame et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The observed footprint size of SYCP3 is similar to that of the DNA-bridging protein H-NS.
source: The observed footprint size of SYCP3, corresponding approximately to one helical turn of DNA, is similar to that of the DNA-bridging protein H-NS that was found to bridge two parallel DNA molecules in register with the helical repeat (Dame et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a comparison to another DNA-bridging protein supported by citation.

claim: A preferential DNA-binding orientation correlated to the DNA helix is supported by the observed value of the 1D-diffusion constant of SYCP3.
source: A preferential DNA-binding orientation correlated to the DNA helix is further supported by the observed value of the 1D-diffusion constant of SYCP3, which is in good agreement with rotation-coupled 1D-sliding along the DNA helix (Blainey et al., 2009).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the diffusion constant measurement supported by citation to a theoretical framework.

claim: In cells, SYCP3-dependent compaction of the meiotic chromosome takes place in the context of chromatin and in the presence of other essential components of chromosome architecture.
source: In cells, SYCP3-dependent compaction of the meiotic chromosome takes place in the context of chromatin and in the presence of other essential components of chromosome architecture, such as other SC proteins, meiotic condensins and cohesins, which likely concur to define the extent of SYCP3-dependent DNA compaction during meiosis.
evidence: This is a statement about the cellular context of SYCP3 function.

claim: Other SC proteins, meiotic condensins and cohesins likely concur to define the extent of SYCP3-dependent DNA compaction during meiosis.
source: In cells, SYCP3-dependent compaction of the meiotic chromosome takes place in the context of chromatin and in the presence of other essential components of chromosome architecture, such as other SC proteins, meiotic condensins and cohesins, which likely concur to define the extent of SYCP3-dependent DNA compaction during meiosis.
evidence: This is an inference about the complexity of the cellular system.

claim: The single-molecule setup is well-suited for analysing systems of increasing complexity, including the addition of lateral element protein SYCP2 and core histones.
source: Although here we limited ourselves to the study of the binary SYCP3-DNA interaction, our single-molecule setup is well-suited for analysing systems of increasing complexity, including for instance the addition of lateral element protein SYCP2 and core histones.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential applications of the experimental approach.

claim: The structure of mitotic chromosomes depends only on a limited number of protein components.
source: The recent finding that the structure of mitotic chromosomes depends only on a limited number of protein components bodes well for future in vitro investigations of meiotic chromosome architecture (Shintomi et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a recent study.

claim: L138 was replaced with cysteine for Alexa555-labelling of SYCP3 via maleimide chemistry.
source: We exploited our knowledge of the SYCP3 structure and the absence of cysteines in its sequence to replace solvent-exposed residue L138, located in the helical core and distant from the N-terminal DNA-binding regions, with cysteine (Figure 2B). The engineered cysteine was linked to the fluorescent dye Alexa555 using maleimide chemistry (Figure 2C), yielding one fluorescent label per helical chain, or four fluorophores per SYCP3 tetramer.
evidence: This describes the labeling strategy used in the experiments.

claim: L138 is exposed to solvent and distant from the DNA-binding domains in the SYCP3 structure.
source: Residue L138 was replaced with cysteine for Alexa555-labelling of SYCP3 via maleimide chemistry. L138 was chosen because it is exposed to solvent and distant from the DNA-binding domains in the SYCP3 structure.
evidence: This explains the rationale for choosing L138 for labeling.

claim: The labeling strategy yielded one fluorescent label per helical chain, or four fluorophores per SYCP3 tetramer.
source: The engineered cysteine was linked to the fluorescent dye Alexa555 using maleimide chemistry (Figure 2C), yielding one fluorescent label per helical chain, or four fluorophores per SYCP3 tetramer.
evidence: This describes the stoichiometry of the labeling.

claim: Mass spectrometry confirmed that all SYCP3 molecules were labelled with Alexa555.
source: Mass spectrometry confirmed that all SYCP3 molecules were labelled with Alexa555, and that the majority of SYCP3 molecules had one label per helical chain (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The majority of SYCP3 molecules had one label per helical chain.
source: Mass spectrometry confirmed that all SYCP3 molecules were labelled with Alexa555, and that the majority of SYCP3 molecules had one label per helical chain (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The experimental setup uses optical tweezers, fluorescence microscopy and microfluidics.
source: Here, we describe a single-molecule assay based on optical tweezers, fluorescence microscopy and microfluidics that, in combination with bulk biochemical data, provides direct visual evidence for our proposed mechanism of SYCP3-mediated chromosome organisation.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The biotinylated ends of a bacteriophage λ DNA molecule are tethered between two streptavidin-coated polystyrene beads that are controlled by focused laser beams acting as optical tweezers.
source: In this system, the biotinylated ends of a bacteriophage λ DNA molecule are tethered between two streptavidin-coated polystyrene beads that are controlled by focused laser beams acting as optical tweezers.
evidence: This describes the experimental setup.

claim: The experiment is performed in a multi-channel laminar flow cell.
source: The experiment is performed in a multi-channel laminar flow cell that allows tethering of DNA to optically-trapped beads and moving the tethered DNA to parallel laminar-flow lanes containing, for example, the fluorescently-labelled components to be analysed (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the experimental setup shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Beam-scanning confocal fluorescence microscopy is used to image the labelled DNA-bound proteins.
source: Beam-scanning confocal fluorescence microscopy is then used to image the labelled DNA-bound proteins.
evidence: This describes the imaging method used.

claim: The average decrease in amplitude of the Gaussian fit associated with bleaching of a single Alexa555 was 1.5 photons per confocal scan-line.
source: The average decrease in amplitude of the Gaussian fit associated with bleaching of a single Alexa555 was 1.5 photons (per confocal scan-line).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of bleaching steps.

claim: The average amplitude of a Gaussian fit for a SYCP3 tetramer is 6.0 photons.
source: This implies that the average amplitude of a Gaussian fit for a SYCP3 tetramer is 6.0 photons.
evidence: This is calculated from the single fluorophore intensity and the number of fluorophores per tetramer.

claim: Under experimental conditions of 6.4 µW excitation intensity, the experiment is dominated by bleaching.
source: Indeed, under experimental conditions of 6.4 µW excitation intensity, the experiment is dominated by bleaching, with a typical rate of 5·10−5s−1 ± 1·10−5 s−1 (sd) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on analysis of bleaching rates at different laser powers.

claim: The typical bleaching rate at 6.4 µW excitation intensity is 5·10−5s−1 ± 1·10−5 s−1.
source: Indeed, under experimental conditions of 6.4 µW excitation intensity, the experiment is dominated by bleaching, with a typical rate of 5·10−5s−1 ± 1·10−5 s−1 (sd) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The average amplitude of a Gaussian fit to each scan line of diffusive trajectories was 5 ± 2 photons.
source: The average amplitude of a Gaussian fit to each scan line of the trajectories was 5 ± 2 photons (sd, N = 8).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of diffusive trajectories.

claim: The average amplitude of diffusive trajectories corresponds to 3.3 ± 1.6 dyes per diffusing trajectory, consistent with the stoichiometry of a single tetramer.
source: Using the calibrated intensity of 1.5 photons for a single dye (see Materials and methods section 'SYCP3 cluster-size determination'), this corresponds to 3.3 ± 1.6 dyes per diffusing trajectory (sd, N = 8), consistent with the stoichiometry of a single tetramer, with a potential slight underestimation related to photobleaching.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the fluorescence intensity data.

claim: The 1D-diffusion coefficient for rotation-coupled sliding is consistent with the observed diffusion constant of SYCP3.
source: A value of D = 0.16 µm2/s can be calculated using, for example, a displacement per helical turn b = 3.4 nm, an average free energy barrier for sliding of ε = 1.33 kBT, and a protein radius of R = 10 nm, which results in a helical path with radius ROC= R + RDNA = 11 nm.
evidence: This is based on theoretical calculations using a model for rotation-coupled diffusion.

claim: The 1D-diffusion coefficient for pure translational motion along the DNA is ~20 fold larger than that for rotation-coupled sliding.
source: Even though this highly simplified model is based on a spherical protein, unlike the elongated shape of SYCP3, the 1D-diffusion coefficient for pure translational motion along the DNA is ~20 fold larger than that for rotation-coupled sliding.
evidence: This is a comparison of theoretical diffusion coefficients for different modes of motion.
